subject: GERM
title: FYS: Images of Otherness
description: The seminar examines images and narratives of the foreign, alien, and uncanny Other in major works of German literature, film, music, and art from Romanticism to the present. Works discussed include Wagner's Lohengrin, expressionist art, and texts by authors such as ETA Hoffmann, Kleist, Freud, Nietzsche, Kafka, and Thomas Mann.

restrictions.text: Open only to newly admitted students in U0 or U1, who may take only one FYS. Students who register for more than one will be obliged to withdraw from all but one of them.

notes: Register for AFYR 101/102 and a foundation seminar OR a writing seminar (not both).

subject: GERM
title: German Language, Intensive Beginners
description: An intensive language course designed to develop communicative skills; covers the first level (GERM 202D1/GERM 202D2) in one term. Required for program students.

subject: GERM
title: German Language, Beginners'
description: A comprehensive first-level course designed to develop communicative skills.

subject: GERM
title: German for Reading
description: Reading German.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken or are taking beginning level courses.

notes: Students must register for both GERM 203D1 and GERM 203D2
No credit will be given for this course unless both GERM 203D1 and GERM 203D2 are successfully completed in consecutive terms

subject: GERM
title: German Holocaust Memory
description: Exploration of the multifaceted dimensions of German Holocaust memory through the examination of texts, artworks, monuments, and debates on memory politics. Delves into the intricate interplay between history, culture, and remembrance in the aftermath of one of the darkest chapters in human history.

subject: GERM
title: Introduction to German Literature 1
description: Introduction to the major authors, genres, and topics of German literature from the Middle Ages to the Age of Goethe, including the Nibelungenlied, Faust, classical tragedy, and the rise of the novel.

subject: GERM
title: Introduction to German Literature 2
description: Introduction to the major authors, genres, and topics of German literature from the 19th century to the present.

subject: GERM
title: German Language Intensive Intermediate
description: Continuation of GERM 200; covers the second level (GERM 307D1/GERM 307D2) in one term.

prerequisites.text: GERM 200 or GERM 202,202D1/D2 or equivalent, or permission of Department

subject: GERM
title: German Language - Intermediate
description: Review of grammar, further development of basic skills; literary and cultural readings.

prerequisites.text: GERM 202 or GERM 200, or equivalent, or permission of Department

subject: GERM
title: German Language - Intensive Advanced
description: This course aims at developing post-intermediate proficiency in listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills, with emphasis on oral and written expression. Special attention is given to word formation and to the proper choice of grammatical structures, vocabulary, and phraseology.

prerequisites.text: GERM 300 or GERM 307D1/D2, or equivalent, or permission of Department.

subject: GERM
title: Topics: German Language and Culture
description: This course aims to both improve students’ speaking and writing skills at the intermediate and advanced levels and to deepen their understanding of German culture through contemporary short texts and films. Topics include migration and national identity, memory and history, gender roles, and intergenerational conflicts. Students develop their transcultural competencies through critical engagement with the course materials. Selected grammatical topics will be reviewed.

prerequisites.text: GERM 307 or equivalent or permission of the Instructor.

corequisites.text: May be taken concurrently with GERM 325 and with permission of the instructor.

subject: GERM
title: Germany after Reunification
description: The events which led to the fall of the Berlin Wall, the reunification of Germany in 1990 and the changing cultural, social, political and economic landscape of the 'New Germany'. Highlighting issues of cultural and social politics, texts discussed include historical, literary and film material.

subject: GERM
title: Topics in Eighteenth-Century German Literature and Culture
description: Study of specific topics as they relate to eighteenth-century German literature and culture.

subject: GERM
title: Science and Literature
description: This course examines the complex exchanges between science and literature across German literature and culture.

subject: GERM
title: German Language, Media and Culture
description: Introduction to German culture through literary and non-literary texts, film, multimedia, commercials, painting and photography. By learning how to read these cultural productions, students will refine their communication skills, expand reading strategies, build vocabulary, and review selective grammatical structures.

subject: GERM
title: Literature and Revolution
description: Seminar on the relationship between literature and political, social and aesthetic change.

subject: GERM
title: Romanticism
description: This course examines one of the pivotal moments of cultural transition in German literary history.

subject: GERM
title: Realism
description: What are the different ways social life has been represented in German literature and culture?

subject: GERM
title: Nature and Ecopoetics
description: This course examines how German literature and culture engage with and construct an understanding of nature and the environment

subject: GERM
title: Modernism and the Avant-Garde
description: This course will focus on the variety of German modernisms and their schools of thought.

subject: GERM
title: Berlin
description: Interdisciplinary study of the quintessential modern centers within Germanic speaking Europe.

subject: GERM
title: German Literature - 19th Century 3
description: This course offers an introduction to the literary movements of Biedermeier, Junges Deutschland, Vormärz, Poetic Realism, and Naturalism in connection with the political and social developments in 19th century Germany. Tests by major authors such as Buchner, Heine and Fontane will be discussed.

subject: GERM
title: Nietzsche and Wagner
description: This course examines the relationship between the philosopher Friedrich Nietzsche and the composer Richard Wagner. It explores their intellectual kinship, their view of art, music, and philosophy in the context of Nietzsche's critique of modernity and decadence and analyzes the Third Reich's and Hollywood's appropriation of Nietzsche and Wagner.

subject: GERM
title: German Culture in European Context
description: A comparative examination of selected moments in German literary, artistic and cultural history in relation to broader European movements; focus on influences, exchanges and dialogues across national boundaries.

prerequisites.text: A culture or literature course at the 200 or 300 level

subject: GERM
title: Franz Kafka
description: This course will look at the works on Franz Kafka, a "classic" modernist author, in three characteristic genres: the story, the novel, and the short prose piece. A selection of Kafka's letters and diary entries as well as critical approaches to his work will also be studied.

subject: GERM
title: German Drama
description: This course will survey the theatrical tradition within German.

subject: GERM
title: Weimar Literature and Culture
description: The course deals with the culture, literature and society of the Weimar Republic and the period of the Third Reich and the Holocaust. Writers studied will include: Brecht, Seghers, Fleisser, Kästner, Tucholsky, Benn, Kolmar, and Lasker-Schüler.

subject: GERM
title: 20th Century Literature Topics
description: Introduction to selected topics and genres in twentieth century literature and culture.

subject: GERM
title: German Postwar Literature
description: The course deals with the literature and culture of the Federal Republic of Germany, the former German Democratic Republic and unified Germany since 1945. It treats major authors and trends. Topics addressed include issues of nationalism and gender, multiculturalism, and other concerns of contemporary German society.

subject: GERM
title: Gender and Society in German Literature and Culture
description: In connection with notions of identity, nationhood, political change, and cultural difference, this course investigates concepts and issues of gender in contemporary German Society. The readings include critical essays and literary texts by writers, scholars, philosophers, journalists, politicians, and political activists.

subject: GERM
title: Modern Short Fiction
description: A study of short prose forms in German throughout history.

subject: GERM
title: Lyric Poetry
description: Introduction to the study of German Poetry from the Middle Ages to the present.

subject: GERM
title: Topics in German Thought
description: A variety of issues significant to the development of German cultural and intellectual life.

subject: GERM
title: Fin-de-Siècle Vienna
description: Interdisciplinary study of one of the formative periods of modern European culture; examination of literature, art, thought, culture and politics in Vienna around 1900.

prerequisites.text: A culture or literature course at the 200 or 300 level

subject: GERM
title: The German Novel
description: Sustained engagement with the major texts of the German novel from Grimmelshausen to the present.

subject: GERM
title: Special Topics in German Film
description: Intensive study of selected topics and periods in German film history.

subject: GERM
title: German Cinema
description: Survey of German cinema from its inception to the present

subject: GERM
title: Topics in German Cinema
description: This course investigates a special topic related to the history of German cinema.

subject: GERM
title: Weimar German Cinema
description: Weimar Cinema brought to the screen a world populated by monsters, lunatics, workers, vamps, strangers, and doubles. These figures embodied the tensions and fears of the Weimar period (1919-1933) in a manner that continues to attract audiences today. This course explores the cultural and political history of the Weimar period through Weimar cinema. It aims to introduce the student to the fundamentals of film analysis, especially formal analysis and textual analysis.

subject: GERM
title: German Media Studies
description: Introduction to the history of German media studies.

subject: GERM
title: German Visual Culture
description: This course engages with the different strands of German visual culture across media.

subject: GERM
title: Topics in German Thought
description: Special topics on German intellectual history and its contributions to major philosophical traditions.

subject: GERM
title: Critical Theory
description: Engagement with the history of critique from Kant to Adorno.

subject: GERM
title: Post-Wall Culture
description: Upper level seminar exploring topics in German culture after unification.

subject: GERM
title: Topics in 21st Century German Literature and Culture
description: Study of pressing contemporary themes within German literature.

subject: GERM
title: Individual Reading Course 01
description: Given solely at the discretion of the instructor.

subject: GERM
title: Internship: German Studies
description: Internship with an approved host institution or organization.

prerequisites.text: Permission of the departmental Internship Advisor.

notes: Open to U2 and U3 students after completing 30 credits of a 90 credit degree program or 45 credits of a 69-120 credit program, a minimum CGPA of 2.7, and permission of the departmental Internship Advisor. This course can only be taken as an elective course. German language proficiency required.

description: Research and completion of the Joint Honours thesis on an approved subject.

restrictions.text: For students in the Joint Honours Program only.

restrictions.text: For students in the Honours Program only.
